title: Single-Implementation Trait (The "Just-in-Case" Trait)
pattern: Defining a trait/interface that has exactly one concrete implementer in the codebase.
why_bad: It adds a layer of indirection, slows down compilation, and complicates refactoring without providing any polymorphic or decoupling benefit. It directly violates YAGNI.
detection: A trait declaration with exactly one `impl` block in both production and test code.
counterexample: Decoupling volatile or non-deterministic external systems (like email or SMS gateways) where mocking/faking is required in tests. Mark the rule `Context-dependent`.
fix: Collapse the trait and let consumers depend directly on the concrete struct.
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (2002), p. 245; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 24.
